newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended lower on Friday but slightly outperformed German Bunds. Profit-taking ahead of the weekend erased initial gains after the fourth Bank of Spain rate cut this year, dealers said.
"This week, our market has been supported by very good domestic news like April inflation and the rate cut. Next week, we will only track foreign bonds," said a BNP trader.
The 10-year spread hit an historic low at 76 basis points and ended at 77 versus 80 at Wednesday's close. The market was closed on Thursday for a holiday.
Chartists saw support for long-term futures, which hit a peak at 116.31 basis points earlier on Friday, at 115.62.
"But (115.62) is not very strong support...The market rose so quickly in the past days," said another.
In the long run, dealers were very bullish, saying they were expecting the Bank of Spain to approve another rate cut soon.
"The next quarter-point rate cut could be delivered as soon as next month," a dealer in Madrid said.
The German proposal to revalue central bank reserve gold as a one-off cash-raising measure to plug the hole in its deficit was largely shrugged off by the Spanish debt market.
"We do not care until it means Germany can't make it and so all the EMU has to be delayed," a dealer said.
On Monday, the National Statistics Institute (INE) will publish its first-quarter employment level survey.
Dealers said bonos were likely to shrug off the data even though there had been relief at drops in jobless rates in recent months.
They said closer attention will be paid to Tuesday's March production index data, expected to show a pick-up in economic activity.
